answer: Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. The island of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a short declarative sentences register, it stays short. The juniper holds work receipts rather than names, so the atlas of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. The design leans on honeypot tasks with known-bad answers, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, every claim is re-checked by someone with nothing to gain.
